subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch

question: Should plugin-runtime session mutations enforce exact owner equality and fail closed on all existing ownerless rows across create, delete, and patch, and should both open PRs be consolidated around one shared helper before either lands?
rationale: Ownerless rows cannot be safely attributed to a plugin, but rejecting them changes upgrade behavior for previously created sessions; repository policy also treats native plugins as one trusted process boundary, so automation cannot choose the intended compatibility-versus-isolation contract.

options.title: Exact ownership everywhere
options.body: Adopt fail-closed exact equality for create, delete, and patch, coordinate both PRs around one helper, and require live upgrade and Gateway proof before merge.

options.title: Preserve ownerless compatibility
options.body: Allow legacy ownerless rows temporarily while rejecting explicit foreign owners, with a documented deprecation or migration plan and tests for both modes.

options.title: Pause both changes
options.body: Defer the ownership expansion until maintainers define the permanent plugin session-ownership and migration contract.

recommendation.title: Exact ownership everywhere
recommendation.body: Adopt fail-closed exact equality for create, delete, and patch, coordinate both PRs around one helper, and require live upgrade and Gateway proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The discussion already identifies this person as the likely owner for the legacy ownerless-session and ownership-boundary choice.
